industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, because the industry is split and the sector rows carry the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Chris Wood (via Jefferies, 17 Oct) would diversify from artificial intelligence into healthcare and financials, and Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, C prior at industry level, with Medtech capital goods at A; but pharmaceuticals against medical technology was not spoken to by any source, clinical-stage biotech is the unproven, cash-burning end the Fragility axis punishes (B.11 at D, relative strength F), and only five of the 149 Pool stocks are healthcare. Pharma/biotech and Hospitals carry B. Counter-case for B at the industry: 94 stocks, the second largest industry, and a defensive rotation that is now five weeks old; for D: a crowded destination.

sector.why: Overweight. Component 1 regime (rates-led late cycle: Richard's view 16-Sep-26, rates and yields rising, inflation high, consumer confidence low, downside skew; sources absent): non-discretionary demand, defensive earnings; relative strength AGREES, A both readings. Counter-case: three stocks, leveraged property-heavy operators are rate-sensitive.

geography.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence for a view named and judged thin. Goldman (19 Oct) names the UK index among those rallying with non-AI, low-beta exposures; its UK Weekly Kickstart 'The Value of Earnings' and the podcast 'The cavalry isn't coming: UK stocks' were titles only; the Bank of England and gilt yields were not read. One clause of index leadership on a 191-stock row, the largest in the table, is not a country view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43). Relative strength is not graded by country. Moves to B if a second source makes the UK case with a rate path read.
